memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt and the Lord your God redeemed you. That is why I give you this command today. And if your servant says to you, "I do not want to leave you," because he loves you and your family and is well off with you, then take an awl and push it through his earlobe into the door, and he will become your servant for life. Do the same for your female servant. - Deut 15:15-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives the deepest reason for treating servants generously: "Remember that you were slaves in Egypt and the Lord your God redeemed you." Israel's own experience of slavery and rescue was meant to shape how they treated others. Having been redeemed by God, they were to extend that same redemptive kindness to those in their care. Memory of God's mercy was the wellspring of their mercy toward others.

Then comes a touching provision. If a servant so loved his master's household that he chose to stay permanently, a mark through the earlobe would signify his willing, lifelong devotion. This was not forced bondage but chosen belonging — a servant who found such goodness in his master's home that he wanted to remain forever. It is a picture of love-driven, willing service, freely given.

There is something here that whispers of the gospel. We were slaves whom God redeemed, and now, having tasted His goodness, we willingly bind ourselves to Him — not out of compulsion, but out of love. Paul repeatedly called himself a "bondservant of Christ Jesus" (Rom 1:1), a title of glad devotion. Having been set free, we choose to belong wholly to the One who loves us, because His service is where we truly flourish. Remembering God's redemption transforms us: it makes us merciful toward others, and it draws us into willing, wholehearted devotion to our good Master. Let the memory of how God rescued you shape both your kindness to others and your glad service to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Does remembering God's redemption shape how I treat others?
- Do I serve God out of glad, willing devotion or reluctant obligation?
- What would it mean to willingly bind myself to God as my good Master?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You redeemed me from slavery, and the memory of Your mercy shapes my heart. Make me merciful toward others as You have been to me. And draw me into glad, willing devotion to You, my good Master, in whose service I truly flourish. Amen.
